finding_under_test: write_sweep_entry refuses any finding_ref already present in the SWEEP ledger, so an entry's reproduced value can never be corrected when the finding's reproducibility later changes

the_measured_defect_is_still_real.the_disagreement: on the committed line '- RUN-1/IMP-002 [CONFIRMED] T-1392 report=buffy-02/saipen_improve_SAIPEN.md reproduced=n', the writer gate improve.validate_sweep (which write_sweep_entry itself calls at improve.py:1030-1036) returns 0 errors and ACCEPTS, while the core validator rejects the same line: 'line 4: RUN-1/IMP-002 CONFIRMED with reproduced=n'. The negative control (the same line with reproduced=y) is ACCEPTED by both.
the_measured_defect_is_still_real.consequence: a disposition can be committed that the core gate reds. That is a real disagreement between two shipped gates, not a cosmetic one.
the_measured_defect_is_still_real.the_refusal_itself_is_correct: the duplicate-finding_ref refusal at improve.py:1004-1011 is doing its job -- a ledger is append-only evidence. The defect is that there is NO verb to amend a value that was wrong when written, so the only way to change reproduced=n to reproduced=y is a hand-edit that bypasses the writer.

why_it_is_held_off.the_dirty_tree_rationale_is_dissolved: the same re-measurement that unblocked T-1394 applies: tools/improve.py's dirty state would need checking, but the earlier blanket rationale ('the SAIPEN repo has 1750 dirty files') is a remembered number, not a fact about the files this fix touches.
why_it_is_held_off.the_real_ground: the fix is TWO things, and neither is a conventional default: (1) a new clause in improve.validate_sweep so the writer gate rejects what the core gate rejects -- this changes what an append-only ledger will accept, in the shared engine; (2) a NEW VERB, `improve sweep --amend`, which is new public API surface in a protocol shared by every project on this machine, with another live session in the same repo. A new verb needs its own design (what evidence does an amendment carry, is the prior line retained or superseded, is it reversible, does it need a lock arm, does it appear in preflight), its own threat model, and its own tests.
why_it_is_held_off.same_class_as_T_1398: both are 'two shipped components disagree and the fix is new surface in a shared engine'. T-1394 was not, because its fix chose which command to NAME and changed no behaviour. The distinction that let T-1394 through is exactly the distinction that holds these two.
